To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) warehouse-computing is a new workload that requires a different set of hardware and software solutions; 2) warehouse-computers have different bottlenecks than traditional data centers; and 3) we can improve performance and cost-efficiency by incorporating non-server-class components into new packaging solutions.

(i) the performance and energy-efficiency of servers can be improved by incorporating non-server-class components and novel packaging, with memory sharing; (ii) a new benchmark suite, based on warehouse-computing, is needed to evaluate next-generation server architectures.
